title: Salary to Hourly Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Salary to Hourly Calculator: Convert an annual salary to an hourly rate — or an hourly wage to a salary. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked…
content:
The [Salary to Hourly Calculator](/salary-to-hourly-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Convert an annual salary to an hourly rate — or an hourly wage to a salary. Enter your convert, amount, hours per week and weeks worked per year and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Convert a salary to an hourly rate, or an hourly wage to a salary, so you can compare job offers on equal terms. The conversion uses your actual working pattern — hours per week and weeks worked per year — because a 40-hour week with two weeks off is not the same as a 50-hour week with none. All figures are gross, before tax and deductions. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Salary to Hourly Calculator

Start by choosing your convert from the list, then entering your amount, entering your hours per week and finally entering your weeks worked per year. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Choose the direction: salary to hourly, or hourly to salary.
2. Enter the amount — the annual salary or the hourly wage.
3. Set your hours per week and weeks worked per year. Adjust the weeks down if you take unpaid time off.
4. Compare the hourly rate with the weekly, monthly and annual figures.

## Formula

Hourly rate = annual salary ÷ (hours per week × weeks per year). Annual salary = hourly wage × hours per week × weeks per year. A standard full-time year is 40 hours × 52 weeks = 2,080 hours.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Salary to Hourly Calculator](/salary-to-hourly-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A $65,000 salary at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks is $31.25 an hour — about $1,250 a week and $5,416.67 a month. The other way, $31.25 an hour at the same hours is $65,000 a year. Try the same figures in the [Salary to Hourly Calculator](/salary-to-hourly-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Convert: Annual salary → hourly rate, Amount: 65000, Hours per week: 40, Weeks worked per year: 52), the [Salary to Hourly Calculator](/salary-to-hourly-calculator) returns Hourly rate: 31.25, Weekly pay: 1,250, Monthly pay: 5,416.67, Annual salary: 65,000. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Comparing job offers

An hourly rate makes offers comparable even when the hours differ. A $70,000 salary at 50 hours a week is $26.92 an hour — less per hour than a $65,000 salary at 40 hours ($31.25). Remember to weigh the whole package too: paid vacation, health cover, retirement matching and bonuses are all part of the real pay, and none of them show up in the hourly rate.

## Overtime and unpaid time off

Salaried roles often include unpaid overtime, which lowers the true hourly rate — divide by the hours you actually work, not the hours in the contract. For hourly roles, unpaid time off lowers the annual total: at 40 hours a week, each unpaid week off costs about 1.9% of the annual salary. Use the weeks-per-year field to model both.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Quick rule: double the hourly rate and add three zeros — $25 an hour is roughly $50,000 a year.
- Contractors: divide your target salary by billable hours (often 1,600–1,800 a year, not 2,080) to set your rate.
- Factor in paid vacation and benefits when comparing offers — they are worth real money.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many working hours are in a year?

A full-time 40-hour week over 52 weeks is 2,080 hours. With two weeks of paid vacation, the working year is 2,000 hours. Try it with your own numbers in the [Salary to Hourly Calculator](/salary-to-hourly-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is this take-home pay?

No, it is gross pay before taxes, retirement contributions and other deductions. Use the Paycheck Calculator to see what you would actually take home. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Salary to Hourly Calculator](/salary-to-hourly-calculator) and start straight away.

### How do I compare a salary with an hourly contract?

Convert both to the same basis — usually the hourly rate for the hours you will actually work — then add the value of benefits, paid time off and job security before deciding. Try it with your own numbers in the [Salary to Hourly Calculator](/salary-to-hourly-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Salary to Hourly Calculator use?

Hourly rate = annual salary ÷ (hours per week × weeks per year). Annual salary = hourly wage × hours per week × weeks per year. A standard full-time year is 40 hours × 52 weeks = 2,080 hours. You can see it in action in the [Salary to Hourly Calculator](/salary-to-hourly-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Salary to Hourly Calculator?

Just Convert, Amount, Hours per week and Weeks worked per year. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
